@GitHub in Slack and Teams just shortened the path from discussion to a pull request.

GitHub announced general availability on November 6. You can investigate a bug, create an issue or request an implementation without leaving the conversation. Teams also has Canvas for reviewing plans, code changes and previews alongside the discussion.

For a small creator or developer team, the value isn't more chat. It's carrying a concrete request into a reviewable change.

Try this week:
Use a connected demo repository. Find one typo in its README. Ask @GitHub: "In [owner/repo], replace [old wording] with [new wording] in README.md. Open a pull request. Do not merge."

Then read the diff. Confirm only the intended wording changed. Run any relevant checks. A person decides whether to merge.

On our latest Tech Thursday, Copilot CLI connected to an image model to generate a batch, and the host still evaluated whether it matched the brief. Different tool surface, same builder responsibility: define the job and inspect the output. We haven't demonstrated this Slack/Teams feature on the show.

The bigger signal: conversations are becoming entry points for workflows. A clear brief and a review boundary make that useful.

Save this for your next small repo change.

Draw from a range of premium looks (do NOT default to the same person-at-a-desk shot every time), for example: a confident Black creator/host presenting direct-to-camera; a close detail of premium creator gear (mic, stream deck, dark walnut desk, the standalone 8 motif on a hoodie or mug); an over-the-shoulder build session; an abstract Afrofuturistic tech or data-visualization environment with glowing electric-blue nodes and grids; or an atmospheric branded studio space. When a person appears they are a confident Black creator, engaged and intentional, never anonymous side profiles. The image should feel like a premium technology documentary and creative studio brand. COMPOSITION FOR TYPOGRAPHY: leave the LOWER-LEFT / lower third of the frame as clean, uncluttered negative space (a dark, simple area with no faces, fine detail, or busy elements there) so a branded headline can be composited over it. SCENE SPECIFICS: Square low architectural view of a single illuminated electric-blue path stopping at a waist-high closed stone review gate in a dark gallery. An adult Black creator's hand rests on a physical release lever at the far right, not yet pulled. The image communicates a deliberate human decision, not a product feature. Deep navy, restrained soft-white gate edge, warm skin highlight; no floating UI. Lower-left remains clear.
